title: The Bridge of Vilna
premise: In 1917, the Baltic trading town of Vilna is requisitioned by an army that seizes the harbor ledgers — including the indenture book holding every diver's name, debts, and family ties. Casper Kavanagh, a pearl diver's daughter indentured since childhood, alone can read the ledger's coded margins, making her indispensable to both the occupying quartermaster and the townsfolk she must decide how to save. As armistice negotiations stall, a single evacuation berth remains, and Casper discovers her long-lost brother and her dying mother are both eligible under its terms. She forges the ledger one final time, naming neither: the berth goes to a stranger's child, and Casper stays behind to keep the town's true record alive, choosing memory over survival.
about_author: Rosalind Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime trade records from the Baltic coast. Her fiction draws on the marginalia of forgotten ledgers, where ordinary people left their only surviving signatures.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Casper Kavanagh dives the cold harbor beds at dawn, trading pearls against a debt she inherited rather than chose. Her POV establishes the town's rhythms and the silences she has learned to keep — especially about her mother's worsening illness. Emotional beat: quiet endurance, the cost of never speaking first.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Army officers arrive and seize the trading company's offices, including the indenture ledger binding every diver family. The company clerk flees; Casper, summoned to translate the coded margin notes only divers understand, realizes the army now holds her community's names. POV: Casper. Beat: dread beneath forced composure.

chapters.title: The Quartermaster's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Quartermaster Aldous Rehn, courteous and watchful, keeps Casper close as his ledger-reader, offering small protections at a price of complicity. She decodes entries that mark families for labor conscription. POV alternates briefly to Rehn, revealing he suspects her loyalty. Beat: the seduction and rot of being useful.

chapters.title: Margins
chapters.summary: Casper secretly copies the ledger at night, discovering her brother Tomas listed alive in a conscript column she'd believed him dead outside of. Grief and hope collide as she weighs telling their dying mother. POV: Casper. Beat: the dangerous gift of information in an occupied town.

chapters.title: What the Divers Know
chapters.summary: The diving families form a silent network around Casper, passing her pearls to bribe guards and asking her to alter the ledger. Each request forces a choice about whose name moves and whose stays. POV shifts to Marta, a fellow diver's wife, showing the town's view of Casper as savior and collaborator alike. Beat: solidarity strained by scarcity.

chapters.title: Armistice Weather
chapters.summary: Rumors of an approaching armistice split the occupiers; Rehn reveals one evacuation berth will be granted before the port closes, selection by ledger eligibility. Casper realizes the rules make both Tomas and her mother eligible — but not both. POV: Casper. Beat: hope arriving as a cruel arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Casper practices altering entries, taught years ago by the old clerk, while Rehn closes in on her night copying. A near-discovery forces her to burn evidence and lie to Marta's face. POV: Casper with a tense interlude from Rehn's suspicion. Beat: guilt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Casper engineers a brief meeting with Tomas among the conscripts; he refuses the berth, insisting it belongs to their mother, while their mother, lucid for one evening, begs Casper to save herself instead. POV: Casper. Beat: love expressed as mutual refusal, each trying to be the sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: As armistice delegates arrive, Rehn confronts Casper with proof of her forgery — but offers her the berth herself if she delivers the ledger intact. In the climax, she forges one final entry naming a drowned stranger's orphaned child, surrenders the doctored ledger, and watches the boat leave without any Kavanagh aboard. Beat: the choice made; duty to memory over blood.

chapters.title: The True Record
chapters.summary: After the armistice, the army withdraws and the company collapses; Casper, unindentured now but unmoored, buries her mother beside the harbor and begins writing the town's real history in the ledger's blank pages — every name, every silence kept. Tomas returns on foot in the last scene. Beat: grief transmuted into witness; survival redefined as remembrance.
